questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Armenia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Administrative divisions” part of the Armenia article.

questions.proof: Armenia is divided into ten provinces, with the city of Yerevan having special administrative status as the country's capital.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Armenia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Armenia article.

questions.proof: They speak both Armenian and their native Kurmanji.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The modern Republic of Armenia became independent in _____ during the dissolution of the Soviet Union.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Armenia article, under the heading “20th century”.

questions.proof: The modern Republic of Armenia became independent in 1991 during the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “By 1920, the state was incorporated into the Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic, and in _____ became a founding member of the Soviet Union.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Armenia article, under the heading “20th century”.

questions.proof: By 1920, the state was incorporated into the Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic, and in 1922 became a founding member of the Soviet Union.
